title: The Apollo program and Campbell's record collection
summary: They recall a program about the Apollo Theater and Campbell's priceless albums.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: You know what I enjoyed? Do you know this thing they did about the Apollo Theater with Frank Albertson?
Oh, yeah, and the Honey Coles and them?

Well, that was really something, that was a program. You know I went to the Apollo -- well, I used to go to the Lafayette and I used to go to the Harlem Opera House and Frank Schiffman -- you see the Apollo used to be a burlesque house. Frank Schiffman took it over -- I don't know whether it's '34 or '35 and I went there for about four years and I missed about five shows in about four years. I saw Count Basie when he came back with the old Benny Morton band, the old Benny Morton brothers. Benny and Al died and then it was the Kansas City Blue Devils and Walter Paige, the bass player. I heard Herschel Evans on tenor and then I heard Lester, and I was telling somebody when Coleman Hawkins left Fletcher Henderson to demonstrate the tenor saxophone around the world, they got Lester Young. Now I got

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.
WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
an album that's priceless. I've got Coleman Hawkins playing "Body and Soul" with strings behind him. "Body and Soul" "Dinner for One Please James" and a lot of the other ballads.
I guess I haven't heard that.

I heard on this Benny Carter album, I played it today and there's a selection on that, I didn't get time to look at it because I was busy doing something else, but there's a passage in fact it sounds just like "One O'Clock Jump" the beginning of "One O'Clock Jump." I forget the title of the tune. It's an old cut, it's one of the early --
